note: The only invented numbers in the estimator. Every entry is an assumption to be replaced by a factor fitted on weighed meals (see calibration.json); none of them is a measurement.

scale_uncertainty.rationale: Relative error of the plate-rim scale (ellipse fit on a SAM mask, a plate diameter typed by hand); enters the 80% range only, counted twice because area goes with scale squared.

solid_density_g_per_ml.rationale: F-004: cooked meat, fish and whole fruit are close to 1.0-1.1 g/mL, while the FNDDS "pieces" cup density (about 0.57) is a chopped-pieces packing density.

oil_levels.label: Sem óleo
oil_levels.rationale: The cook used no added oil: none of the class default is added.

oil_levels.label: Pouco
oil_levels.rationale: Half of the class default oil (default_oil_g_per_100g); a guess at what a light hand means.

oil_levels.label: Normal
oil_levels.rationale: The class default oil per 100 g of food, as in the nutrition table entry.

oil_levels.label: Muito
oil_levels.rationale: Double the class default oil; a guess at what a heavy hand means.

typical_plate.rationale: Used when the plate is not a registered one: a common flat dinner plate is about 26 cm across.
typical_plate.calibrate_from: the owner's plates and the benchmark

typical_plate_scale_uncertainty.rationale: Plate diameters in homes range roughly 22 to 30 cm, so an unknown plate is a wider scale error than a measured one; replaces scale_uncertainty in the range (counted twice, as for a known plate).
typical_plate_scale_uncertainty.calibrate_from: the owner's plates and the benchmark

no_plate_scale_uncertainty.rationale: When no plate is found the food region is assumed to span a typical plate, which can be off by a third either way (a half-empty plate, a large platter); wider than the typical plate's own uncertainty, and replaces scale_uncertainty in the range (counted twice).
no_plate_scale_uncertainty.calibrate_from: photos where the plate is not found, weighed on a scale

calibration.note: How the app learns from scale checks (web/estimate/calibration.mjs). All three are assumptions about how fast to trust a few weighings; they are tuned on the checks themselves.

shrinkage_k.rationale: Pseudo-checks that pull a learned factor toward 1 (or a group factor toward the global one): with n checks the learned log-correction is weighted n/(n+5), so 5 checks give half of what they measured.

group_min_checks.rationale: N: a food group gets its own factor only after this many item checks in that group; before that it uses the global factor.

conformal_min_checks.rationale: M: conformal 80% ranges replace the model-based ones only after this many checks; the quantile needs at least 4 residuals to exist at all and is noisy with few.

autoseg.note: Thresholds of the automatic plate and food detection (web/estimate/autoseg.mjs). All are guesses to be tuned on the owner's phone and on the benchmark with tap-mode outlines as the oracle.

plate_grid_n.rationale: A 5 x 5 grid of point prompts (25 decodes) is coarse on purpose: the plate is large, so few points hit it.

food_grid_n.rationale: An 8 x 8 grid (about 40 points fall inside a plate ellipse) trades decode time for recall of small foods.
food_grid_n.calibrate_from: phone timing and recall on the benchmark

decode_batch.rationale: Points decoded between time-budget checks and progress updates. Each point is its own decoder run (T-017: SAM 2.1 takes one prompt group per run, so runs are not batched); larger chunks check the budget less often.

time_budget_ms.rationale: Total decode time allowed per photo before the grid stops early and uses the masks found so far.

masks_per_point.rationale: Keep only the best-scoring of the three masks SAM returns for each point; dedupe handles the rest.

plate_masks_per_point.rationale: The plate grid keeps all three masks SAM returns per point: the best-scoring one is often a part of the plate or the plate without its food, and the whole plate is only one of the outputs (T-017).

mask_side.rationale: Auto mode works on masks whose long side is this many pixels, read straight from SAM's 256x256 low-res logits (bilinear), instead of full-photo float masks: SAM has no finer detail than its logits, and full-size masks for ~90 decodes killed the Safari tab on the iPhone 16e (T-017). The chosen plate and foods are resized to the photo afterwards.
mask_side.calibrate_from: the model integration test (low-res vs full-size mask IoU) and iPhone memory

crash_retry.rationale: When the previous analysis closed the page (the browser ran out of memory), the retry uses fewer prompts and smaller masks.

naming_page_plans.rationale: Backends for the naming model in auto mode's naming page on the iPhone, one plan per attempt (a death in that page moves the retry to the next plan). The owner's third run died loading the naming model on WebGPU in the fresh naming page right after the SAM page (GPU memory likely not yet given back), so the CPU (CLIP image tower 64 MB q4, 89 MB q8; 224 px input, small activations) is tried first; WebGPU q4f16 ran on the 16e when alone (feasibility run 3).

plate_support_iou.rationale: Among the masks that pass as a plate, the plate is the one most others agree with (bounding-box IoU and area ratio at least this): SAM returns the real plate from many grid prompts, while a table band or placemat around it passes the ring test from one or two. Largest on a tie. The first real-model run chose a 0.88-of-photo band over a 0.43 plate seen by ~30 prompts when the largest candidate won.

plate_ring_min_arc.rationale: SAM often returns a plate rim as a ring around the food that does not quite close. Its convex hull is taken as the plate when the ring reaches at least this share of the angular sectors around the hull's ellipse (a placemat cross or a heap of food reaches far fewer).

plate_ring_min_band.rationale: A plate rim is a band along the plate edge: at least this share of a ring's pixels must lie in the rim band (radius plate_ring_band_lo to 1.1 of the hull ellipse). A placemat cross or a heap of food can reach every sector but most of it is inside or outside that band.

plate_ring_band_lo.rationale: Inner radius, as a share of the hull ellipse, of the boundary band in which a ring must have pixels: a plate rim is a band along the edge, not a thin line.

plate_ring_sectors.rationale: Number of equal angular sectors used to measure how far around the plate a ring reaches.

noplate_center_frac.rationale: When no plate is found, foods are looked for on the grid points inside this central share of the photo (width and height), where the meal is when nobody taps.
noplate_center_frac.calibrate_from: photos where the plate is not found

noplate_span_factor.rationale: With no plate, the food region is assumed to span a typical plate: the circle standing in for the plate has the radius of the food region's moment ellipse times this factor (a plate is a little larger than the food on it).
noplate_span_factor.calibrate_from: photos where the plate is not found, weighed on a scale

noplate_default_plate_frac.rationale: With no plate and no food found, the stand-in plate is a circle of this share of the short side of the photo, at its centre.
noplate_default_plate_frac.calibrate_from: photos where the plate is not found

noplate_food_min_image_frac.rationale: With no plate there is no plate area to compare with: a food mask smaller than this share of the photo is noise or a crumb.
noplate_food_min_image_frac.calibrate_from: photos where the plate is not found

noplate_food_max_image_frac.rationale: With no plate, a mask covering more than this share of the photo is the table or the background, not a food (a mask touching two photo edges is also refused).
noplate_food_max_image_frac.calibrate_from: photos where the plate is not found

dedupe_iou.rationale: From ADR 0005: two masks overlapping more than this are the same object and the lower predicted IoU is dropped.

plate_min_area_frac.rationale: A plate photographed inside the frame covers at least about an eighth of the photo.

plate_max_area_frac.rationale: A mask covering nearly the whole photo is the table or the background, not a plate.

plate_center_frac.rationale: Side of the central box of the photo (as a fraction of width and height) that the plate must cover.

plate_center_cover_min.rationale: At least half of the central box must lie inside the plate mask, so a plate off to the side or a napkin in the centre is not chosen.

plate_max_residual.rationale: 1 minus the IoU between the mask and its moment-fitted ellipse: SAM plate masks fit an ellipse to within about 10 percent; a table or a rectangle fits worse.

food_min_frac.rationale: From ADR 0005: a food smaller than 0.5% of the plate area is noise or a crumb.

food_max_frac.rationale: From ADR 0005: a mask covering more than 85% of the plate is the plate itself, not a food.

food_min_pred_iou.rationale: SAM's own predicted IoU below this means an unstable mask (a part of a food or a smear).

food_min_inside_frac.rationale: At least this share of a food mask must lie on the plate; the rest is a table, a hand or a glass.

merge_adjacency_px.rationale: Fragments of one food with the same name closer than this many pixels (Chebyshev, working photo) are merged into one item.

max_food_items.rationale: A plate rarely holds more than 8 distinct foods; more is over-segmentation, and the smallest are dropped.

non_food_labels.rationale: From ADR 0005: what a mask that is not food is called; a mask whose best SigLIP label is one of these is dropped.

food_grid_inset.rationale: Food prompts are placed inside an ellipse shrunk to 95% of the plate so rim points do not prompt the plate itself.

rice_pasta.rationale: A plated heap of rice or pasta is about 2 cm tall on average; heaps vary a lot between people.

beans_stews.rationale: Beans and stews are ladled as a shallow layer, roughly 1.5 cm deep, and spread into the rice.

mash_layered.rationale: Mashed, layered or baked starch dishes sit as a thick slab or mound of about 2.5 cm.

starchy_pieces.rationale: Potato, cassava and corn pieces are about one piece thick when spread, roughly 2.5 cm.

loose_meat.rationale: Minced meat is spooned as a low mound of about 1.5 cm.

cooked_veg.rationale: Cooked or sauteed vegetables are a pile of about 2 cm; leaves collapse, chunks do not.

salad_raw.rationale: Raw salad is a loose pile whose height is set by the leaves, about 2.5 cm and very variable.

cutlet_meat.rationale: A grilled steak, cutlet or breaded fillet is about 1.5 cm thick.

thick_meat.rationale: Thick cuts, patties, bone-in pieces and sausages are about 2.5 cm through the middle.

fish_seafood.rationale: Fish fillets and shrimp are about 1.5 cm thick.

egg.rationale: A fried egg is about 1 cm and a boiled egg about 4 cm; 2 cm is the compromise.

whole_fruit.rationale: Whole fruit is roughly 4 cm thick (banana about 3.5 cm, apple or orange 6 cm, berries 2 cm).

sliced_fruit.rationale: Fruit slices and chunks are about 2.5 cm thick.

cheese_slice.rationale: A cheese slice is about 0.8 cm thick.

spread_sauce.rationale: Yogurt and mayonnaise are a dollop or spread of about 1.2 cm, and the amount is highly variable.
